item.text:
Using your local prior as the structured baseline, and not touching the client matrix, here is the compact research frame for Bongbong Marcos in 2022.

**Office, Authority, Constraints**
- Marcos was proclaimed president-elect on **May 25, 2022** and sworn in on **June 30, 2022**. That makes **June 30, 2022** the start of the ruler period for 2022.
- His office is the Philippine presidency. Under **Article VII of the 1987 Constitution**, executive power is vested in the President, the term begins at **noon on June 30**, and the President has control over executive departments and offices.
- A concrete example of that authority is **Executive Order No. 1** on **June 30, 2022**, which reorganized the Office of the President and abolished the Presidential Anti-Corruption Commission and the Office of the Cabinet Secretary.
- The main constraints are structural: Congress, the courts, the budget process, local governments, treaty obligations, and the inherited economy/security environment. The local prior already covers the country-year indicators for rights, corruption, governance, conflict, and welfare, so I did not re-fetch those structured datasets.

**Inherited Conditions / Major 2022 Context**
- Post-pandemic recovery was incomplete.
- Inflation and joblessness were immediate economic priorities.
- The Duterte-era human-rights and press-freedom controversies remained live issues.
- The Philippines also faced South China Sea tensions and repeated disaster exposure, especially typhoons.

**Retained Source Set**
I kept 12 sources total, balancing primary/legal, favorable state-media, independent wire, local-language, and critical families.

| Source | Use | Fit / attribution / limits |
|---|---|---|
| [1987 Constitution, Article VII](https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/3/353) - Supreme Court E-Library, 1987 | Legal baseline for office, term, and executive power | Best source for formal authority and constraints. Direct constitutional text. Limitation: says what the presidency can do in law, not how Marcos used the office in practice. |
| [Marcos, Duterte proclaimed winners in PH’s fastest vote count](https://www.pna.gov.ph/index.php/articles/1175224) - Philippine News Agency, May 25, 2022 | Mandate / transition point | Congress officially proclaimed Marcos president-elect with 31,629,783 votes. Good chronology for the start of the transition. Limitation: government-friendly proclamation coverage, not an independent audit of the broader election debate. |
| [Marcos Jr. sworn in as PH's 17th president](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1177892) - Philippine News Agency, June 30, 2022 | Start of rule period | Marcos took the oath before Chief Justice Gesmundo at the National Museum on June 30, 2022. Best for pinning the ruler period precisely. Limitation: ceremonial, official framing. |
| [Executive Order No. 1](https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/5/95382) - Supreme Court E-Library, June 30, 2022 | Early exercise of executive power | Shows Marcos invoking Article VII control and reorganization authority; it abolished the PACC and Cabinet Secretary office. Strong evidence of how he moved immediately. Limitation: self-justifying executive text; effectiveness is not established by the order itself. |
| [Marcos delivers ‘data-driven’ SONA](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1179738) - Philippine News Agency, July 25, 2022 | Core 2022 policy agenda | First SONA centered on economic recovery, COVID response, return to face-to-face classes, legislative priorities, and sovereignty in the South China Sea. This is the best single official summary of his 2022 governing agenda. Limitation: speech coverage, not implementation. |
| [Philippines' Marcos signals continuity ahead with new economic team](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/philippines-marcos-names-new-finance-chief-and-central-bank-governor-2830330) - Reuters, May 25, 2022 | Inherited economic conditions | Reuters framed Marcos as inheriting a stronger economy than the late-Marcos era, but with inflation and joblessness as immediate priorities. Good pre-inauguration context for 5B and 8B. Limitation: pre-office analysis; not a performance score. |
| [Summary Inflation Report Consumer Price Index (2018=100): September 2022](https://psa.gov.ph/content/summary-inflation-report-consumer-price-index-2018100-september-2022) - Philippine Statistics Authority, October 5, 2022 | Objective macro pressure | Official inflation release: 6.9% headline inflation in September 2022 and 5.1% year-to-date. Useful for inherited conditions and early-term pressure. Limitation: national aggregate, not ruler-specific causality. |
| [Typhoon makes Philippine landfall, government work suspended](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/philippines-evacuates-coasts-cancels-sea-trips-as-supertyphoon-nears-2898341) - Reuters, September 24/25, 2022 | Major 2022 event / disaster response | Marcos suspended government work and classes as Noru hit Luzon; thousands were evacuated. Useful for state-capacity context and emergency response. Limitation: weather shock, not a direct governance choice. |
| [World Report 2023: Philippines](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2023/country-chapters/philippines) - Human Rights Watch, 2023 | Critical rights narrative | HRW says the human-rights situation hardly changed after Marcos took office, citing continued drug-war killings, red-tagging, and journalist harassment. Strong chapter 3B/4B/7B counterweight. Limitation: advocacy lens, not neutral statistics. |
| [Philippines: Decision to not rejoin the ICC statute will not prevent investigation](https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa35/5936/2022/en/) - Amnesty International, August 10, 2022 | Accountability / impunity | Records Marcos’ statement that the Philippines had no intention of rejoining the ICC and Amnesty’s view that domestic investigations were not genuine. Useful for 3B and 7B. Limitation: advocacy/legal position; contested by the government. |
| [CPJ calls on President-elect Marcos to protect press freedom in the Philippines](https://cpj.org/2022/05/cpj-calls-on-president-elect-marcos-to-protect-press-freedom-in-the-philippines/) - Committee to Protect Journalists, May 23, 2022 | Press-freedom warning | Pre-inauguration warning to reverse Duterte-era harassment, protect Rappler, and restore press freedom. Good for framing inherited media constraints. Limitation: advocacy letter, predictive rather than descriptive. |
| [Mandatory ROTC sa mga estudyante, ibabalik ni Pangulong Marcos](https://radyo.inquirer.net/318520/mandatory-rotc-sa-mga-estudyante-ibabalik-ni-pangulong-marcos) - DZIQ Radyo Inquirer 990AM, July 25, 2022 | Local-language family / domestic framing | Filipino-language reporting on a first-SONA proposal to make ROTC mandatory again for senior high school. This is the local-language source family I retained. Limitation: one outlet’s report of a proposal; implementation remained uncertain and politically contested. |

**Compact Event Map**
- **May 25, 2022**: Congress proclaims Marcos president-elect.
- **June 30, 2022**: Marcos is sworn in as the 17th President; EO No. 1 is issued the same day.
- **July 25, 2022**: First SONA sets the agenda around recovery, COVID, education, infrastructure, and sovereignty.
- **August 10, 2022**: Amnesty says the ICC non-rejoin decision will not block investigation.
- **September 24-26, 2022**: Typhoon Noru/Karding hits; Marcos orders work/class suspensions and aid response.
- **October 5, 2022**: PSA reports inflation at 6.9% in September.
- **Late 2022**: HRW’s year-end review says the rights environment remained largely unchanged, with continued killings, red-tagging, and press pressure.

**Chapter Source Plan**
- **1B**: No retained ruler-specific source. If you later need non-attributable nuclear background only, use SIPRI/NTI/WNA as background, not as ruler evidence.
- **2B**: PNA proclamation, PNA inauguration, Reuters economic context, Reuters typhoon response.
- **3B**: HRW, Amnesty, CPJ, plus your local prior’s CIRIGHTS/PTS/UCDP/V-Dem facts.
- **4B**: Constitution, EO No. 1, PNA SONA, and the local-language Radyo Inquirer SONA report.
- **5B**: Reuters economic inheritance, PSA inflation, and the local prior’s GDP/population facts.
- **6B**: Mostly your local prior on health, education, HDI, and life expectancy; add SONA references only if you need narrative justification.
- **7B**: EO No. 1, HRW, Amnesty, CPJ, and the local prior’s corruption/accountability/rule-of-law facts.
- **8B**: Constitution, EO No. 1, PNA SONA, Reuters economy, and the local prior’s governance-capacity facts.

If you want, I can turn this into a chapter-by-chapter evidence dossier next, still without scoring.
